Hi Vivek,

As we ramp the pilot we need a concise statement of commitments and evidence on three items so our security/compliance board can greenlight production ingress: 

1) Residency guarantee: can Redwood commit to storing and processing Nova pilot data exclusively within US regions (no cross-border backups or failover outside the US) for the trial period? Please spell out what you can commit contractually vs operationally.

2) Private connectivity: we need a diagram and short description of the PrivateLink/privatelink-style connectivity options you offer (VPC peering, PrivateLink, customer-managed VPN), plus whether traffic ever transits public internet between Nova and model-hosting.

3) Evidence pack: SOC 2 summary, SIG/CAIQ mapping (we prefer a completed CAIQ CSV or link), and an ops-runbook stub describing how you isolate tenant keys and snapshots.

Could you provide a single PDF with a short one-page commitment letter, plus any topology diagram and a SOC2 summary? If you have a standard attestation template you can sign, that would speed approvals.

We'd like this by Wednesday EOB ET if possible to keep the pilot schedule.

Thanks,
Elise
Elise Harper
Head of Cloud Security, Nova Health

Hi Elise — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. High level answers up front, with artifacts and a single PDF to follow in my next message: 

- Residency guarantee: For the pilot we can commit operationally and contractually to US-only processing and storage. Our standard pilot SLA addendum and data residency rider restricts primary and backup storage to US regions and disables cross-border snapshot replication. We'll attach the signed-commitment template.

- Private connectivity: Redwood supports customer-controlled PrivateLink (AWS), VPC peering (where customers own the VPC), and IPsec VPN tunnels. When PrivateLink is used, traffic does not traverse the public internet: connections are endpoint-to-endpoint within the cloud provider's private network. I'll attach a concise topology diagram showing where model serving sits, where KV caches are kept, and the peering/privatelink endpoints.

- Evidence pack: We'll provide a SOC 2 summary, completed CAIQ mapping (CSV), and a short ops runbook that explains KMS key scoping, snapshot retention, and cross-region replication controls. The CAIQ will have answers flagged where additional legal wording is recommended.

Operational notes / limitations:
- High-availability failover between regions (e.g., US-east -> US-west) is supported but we will not enable cross-border (US <-> EU) snapshot replication for Nova's pilot unless explicitly requested.
- If Nova requires customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS), we can integrate with your AWS KMS through a cross-account key policy; when that is in place, Redwood does not hold plaintext material.

Next steps: I'll pull the requested artifacts and send a consolidated PDF + diagrams within 24 hours. If you prefer we can lock in a 30-minute call tomorrow morning ET to walk the packet.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek — that helps. A couple of clarifying questions before you send the pack: 

- KMS origin: when you say "cross-account key policy" — will the CMEK be controlled fully by Nova (we need an assurance that Redwood cannot decrypt snapshots), and how are ephemeral keys handled for inference caching?
- Backups/snapshots: are automated EBS/RDS-style snapshots ever replicated outside the configured region due to provider-level backup policies or DR playbooks?
- Logs & forensics: do you retain any debug traces that may include customer payloads outside the US for debugging/ops? If so what is your retention window and can we opt-out?

If you can call out these three points in the evidence PDF with short, bullet answers, that will make our info-sec review faster. We can do the 30-minute call tomorrow at 10am ET if that works for your team.

Elise

Elise — attached is the consolidated evidence packet we discussed. Summary below and included artifacts:

Attachments (short stubs included in packet):
- redwood-region-commitment.pdf — one-page signed commitment (pilot rider) that restricts primary storage, backups, and snapshots to US regions for the term defined.
- privatelink-topology.png — single-page diagram: Nova VPC -> AWS PrivateLink endpoint -> Redwood model-serving VPC; shows KMS boundary and where KV cache lives.
- soc2-summary.pdf — SOC 2 Type II scope summary and link to our auditors' summary; includes date range and controls relevant to data locality.
- caiq-mapping.csv (included inside the consolidated zip) — completed CAIQ with flags on items that require contract language.

Explicit answers to your three questions: 
- KMS origin: we support CMEK via cross-account AWS KMS. With CMEK, Nova controls the key policy: Redwood operators do not have permission to decrypt snapshots or live volumes. Ephemeral inference cache keys are KMS-generated, short-lived, and do not persist outside the encrypted volume; we include the cache lifecycle in the ops runbook.
- Backups/snapshots: automated snapshots are restricted to the configured US region for the pilot. We do not enable cross-region replication. Provider-managed backups (rare maintenance snapshots) are documented in the runbook and are disabled for pilot tenants unless explicitly requested and contractually agreed.
- Logs & forensics: we retain operational logs (non-payload) for 90 days by default in US-only storage. Payload-level debug traces are not retained by default; if collection is required for debugging, it is opt-in with a signed change request and limited retention (30 days) unless Nova requests otherwise.

Links and next steps:
- CAIQ mapping and SOC2 summary are in the consolidated ZIP: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cSIG-CAIQ-mapping
- Privatelink runbook excerpt: https://redwood.example.com/privatelink-runbook

Please reply if the rider and attachments are sufficient for your board; otherwise we can execute the standard pilot rider via DocuSign. Confirming the 10am ET call — Kimberly and Irene will join to walk the topology and KMS flow.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
